gap: No result ChatGPT got states energy per pound. Dividing each pack's Wh by its weight gives about 62 Wh/lb for the 100Ah budget packs (Redodo kit 5,120 Wh / 82 lb; LiTime 200A Bluetooth 5,120 Wh / 82 lb) and 49.8 Wh/lb for the Allied RS 48V 105Ah that ChatGPT called its premium pick (5,376 Wh / 108 lb). That means Allied's $2,699.99 pack carries 26 lb more battery than the Redodo for 256 Wh more energy.
standout_why: I compared the two cited pages (golfcartshowdown.com and golfcartbatterysource.com), golfcartgearlab.com, canyonlakemobile.com and our own dealectric.com page. golfcartshowdown lists pack weights (Eco Gen3 98 lb, Bolt 101 lb, Allied Big Box 108 lb, Dakota 77 lb) and computes $/kWh, but never divides energy by weight. golfcartbatterysource has weights, $/kWh stored and maker charge times in a table, but no Wh/lb. golfcartgearlab and canyonlakemobile give no pack weights. Our own page already has $/kWh, charge hours (Ah ÷ charger A) and continuous kW, but no weights. So the rivals hold some of the inputs, and none of them computes Wh/lb. $/kWh and charge time are already covered by both a cited rival and our page, so they add nothing new.
decides: It supports ChatGPT's 'best value' lean toward the 100Ah complete kits over Allied. Redodo's kit at $1,149.99 has the best energy per pound and the lowest price per kWh: 5,120 Wh / 82 lb = 62.4 Wh/lb, and $1,149.99 / 5.12 kWh = $225/kWh. Allied RS is the heaviest per Wh at 49.8 Wh/lb and costs about $502/kWh. Allied's price buys warranty and brand, not energy density. The pick for hilly or lifted carts still depends on continuous amps, not Wh/lb. Also, LiTime's kit is now $1,154.66, not the $1,281.66 ChatGPT showed.
